text: Thenar pays people to record robot arm demonstrations, and sells what they record as training data for physical AI. This is the whole loop, live on testnets.
Thenar's arm is a six-axis robot that anyone can drive from a browser.
The hub lists open tasks. Each one is a bounty held in escrow in USDC on Arc, and each accepted run is paid on the spot.
At the station, the arm moves objects into a target circle. A trained policy is driving here, so this is a practice run.
When the object settles, the run is measured for placement, smoothness and time. A practice run is scored, and never submitted.
Robotics labs fund the bounties. A lab's budget sits in a Privy server wallet, with a Privy policy that only lets it fund Thenar tasks on Arc.
We post a one cent bounty from that budget. Privy signs it under the policy, and the transaction is being signed and confirmed on Arc now.
Arcscan shows it confirmed: the lab wallet paying into the Thenar protocol contract.
Now we ask the same wallet to send one cent anywhere else. Privy's policy engine refuses, and nothing is signed.
The recordings are sold to AI agents. An agent asks for a task's data, and the server answers with HTTP 402, Payment Required, priced in HBAR on Hedera.
First, World AgentKit asks AgentBook on World Chain whether a verified human stands behind the agent. This agent is not registered, so it pays.
The agent signs a Hedera transfer of half an HBAR, and the Blocky402 facilitator settles it. The transaction is being signed and confirmed on Hedera now.
On HashScan, the agent's Hedera account pays the corpus treasury account, and the facilitator pays the fee.
Every sale is written to a Hedera Consensus Service topic, with the SHA-256 of the exact file served, so the buyer can check its own copy.
Follow the value. A person's run is scored and paid on Arc. An agent pays for the data on Hedera. And the file's fingerprint lands on a topic only the seller can write to.
The corpus itself is a security, issued through Hedera's Asset Tokenization Studio: Thenar Robot Corpus, with a whitelist of holders.
The issuer now issues ten new shares into the treasury reserve. The transaction is being signed and confirmed on Hedera now.
HashScan shows the issuance on the security's contract, and the supply on Thenar moves up by ten.
Holding a share needs a place on the whitelist. The agent's wallet has none, so the security itself refuses it, with Account Is Blocked.
These are the three transactions from this recording: the bounty on Arc, the data sale on Hedera, and the share issuance through the Tokenization Studio.

The easy attack on a bounty market is one person with a hundred wallets. Thenar signs a run only after a World ID Selfie Check, one per human, bound to one wallet. In this recording, a wallet with no proof was refused before anything was paid.
On Arc, all ten Thenar contracts are deployed and source-verified, each linked from the contracts page.
The status page checks the live system every fifteen seconds: the verifier key, the contract, the database and the chain.
People record the data, Arc pays them, Hedera sells it and tokenizes it, and World keeps it to one person per set of runs. Thanks for watching Thenar.
